![](edge-clustering_files/figure-html/fig-payoff-1.png){#fig-payoff width=672}
:::
:::


This is the posterior co-clustering matrix of the 17 Wenchuan PTSD
symptoms: each cell is the share of posterior draws in which two
symptoms landed in the same cluster. There is visible texture, with
the intrusion and arousal symptoms shading darker together than the
avoidance items between them, but it stays texture: even the lightest
pairs co-cluster in 57 percent of draws, every symptom's modal
allocation is the same single cluster, and the posterior puts
probability 0.42 on there being no clusters at all. The model's answer
to "do these symptoms form communities?" is that these data do not
say. That verdict is the page: a clustering claim that comes with its
own evidence and its own uncertainty, including the honest case where
the evidence is thin.

The usual route to communities is post-hoc: estimate a network, then
run a community detection algorithm on the point estimate. That
returns a partition, always, with no statement of how sure to be about
it, and no way to conclude that there is *no* community structure. The
stochastic block model (SBM) edge prior instead makes the clustering
part of the graphical model: cluster assignments, the number of
clusters, and the evidence for clustering against no clustering are
all estimated together with the network, so every cluster statement
arrives with a posterior probability attached
[@SekulovskiEtAl_2025_sbm].

## The fit


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(bgms)

fit = bgm(Wenchuan, edge_prior = sbm_prior(), seed = 123)
```
:::


The [Wenchuan](../reference/datasets.qmd#wenchuan) data ship with the
package: 17 ordinal PTSD symptom items from 362 survivors of the 2008
Wenchuan earthquake. Apart from the edge prior and the seed this is
[`bgm()`](../reference/bgm.qmd) at its defaults, and
[`sbm_prior()`](../reference/priors.qmd#sbm_prior) is itself at its
defaults, with `lambda = 1`: a prior expectation of two clusters, and
prior probability $\exp(-1) \approx 0.37$ on no clustering at all. The
run takes several minutes. The guide's
[Edge Clustering](../guide/clustering.qmd) page carries the model and
the hyperparameter guidance, including settings for when clustering is
expected and when the goal is to protect against false positive
clusters.

## Read the clustering

Everything cluster-related lives in one extractor,
[`extract_sbm()`](../reference/extractors.qmd#extract_sbm). Its first
component is the posterior over the number of clusters:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sbm = extract_sbm(fit)
round(head(sbm$posterior_num_blocks, 4), 3)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  probability
1       0.421
2       0.362
3       0.156
4       0.049
```


:::
:::


The rows are numbers of clusters: probability 0.42 on one cluster,
0.36 on two, 0.16 on three, and a thin tail beyond. The test of
clustering against no clustering compares the posterior odds of $B >
1$ with the prior odds, which under the shifted-Poisson prior are
$\exp(\lambda) - 1$:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p1 = sbm$posterior_num_blocks["1", "probability"]
((1 - p1) / p1) / (exp(1) - 1)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.801806
```


:::
:::


A Bayes factor of about 0.80: essentially no evidence either way. The
pointwise comparison of one cluster against two (prior odds one at
`lambda = 1`, so the Bayes factor is the ratio of the two posterior
probabilities) is about 1.16, just as undecided. These data neither
support block structure among the PTSD symptoms nor rule it out; both
tests and their prior odds are derived in the guide's
[Testing for clustering](../guide/clustering.qmd#testing-for-clustering)
section.

The allocations tell the same story:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
table(sbm$posterior_mode_allocations)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 1 
17 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
cm = sbm$posterior_mean_coclustering_matrix
round(range(cm[upper.tri(cm)]), 2)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.57 0.91
```


:::
:::


All 17 symptoms share one modal cluster, and the co-clustering shares
range from 0.57 to 0.91: high everywhere, sharp nowhere. That is what
the figure at the top of the page shows; it was drawn from the
extractor's co-clustering matrix directly:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p = nrow(cm)
op = par(mar = c(6.5, 6.5, 1, 1))
image(1:p, 1:p, cm[, p:1], col = hcl.colors(20, "Blues", rev = TRUE),
      axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
axis(1, at = 1:p, labels = rownames(cm), las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7)
axis(2, at = p:1, labels = colnames(cm), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
par(op)
```
:::


In a dataset with real block structure this plot shows distinct dark
diagonal blocks of variables that always cluster together, and the
modal allocations split into groups. Report the two together: a
partition without its co-clustering matrix hides exactly the
uncertainty this analysis exists to expose.

## The edges still get verdicts

The SBM prior is an edge prior, so the fit is still a full analysis of
the network itself, and every tool from the earlier pages applies:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
table(verdicts(fit)$verdict)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 presence undecided   absence 
       32        32        72 
```


:::
:::


These counts differ a little from the ones in
[From estimation to evidence](estimation-to-evidence.qmd) (32
supported, 32 undecided, 72 ruled out here, against 35, 39, and 62
there); that fit used the default Bernoulli edge prior and a longer
run, so this is not a controlled comparison of priors. The point is
smaller and worth knowing: the edge prior is part of the model, and
the inclusion Bayes factors inherit it.

## What a cluster is not

A cluster here is structure in edge *inclusion probabilities* under
this prior: symptoms in the same block are modeled as more likely to
share edges with each other than with the rest. It is not a causal
module, not a latent factor, and not a clinical subscale; none of
those readings are licensed by a partition of a partial association
structure. And an uncertain clustering is not a failed analysis. On
these data the model was free to find blocks and did not, which is a
finding in itself, and a caution against over-reading the apparent
groupings that any network drawing produces by placing connected nodes
near each other.

## What to report

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What to report

- The clustering test with the prior it rests on: "The Bayes factor
  for clustering against no clustering was
  $\text{BF} = \texttt{<value>}$ under `sbm_prior()` with
  $\lambda = \texttt{<value>}$," and its verdict: support, evidence
  against, or, as here, undecided.
- If clusters are supported: the posterior over the number of
  clusters, the modal allocations, and the co-clustering matrix (or
  its range) as the uncertainty statement for the partition.
- The hyperparameters, if changed from the defaults: they encode how
  strongly the prior expects clustering.
- Not licensed: reading groups in a network drawing as clusters,
  reporting a partition without its allocation uncertainty, or
  reading a Bayes factor near one as evidence that there are no
  clusters.
:::
